So we need to assign to each person a hobby (cooking or chess), a job (engineer or chef), a nationality (thai or canadian) such that each attribute's two values appear exactly once across the two persons.

1. "The person who is a engineer is not anywhere to the left of the person who likes chess". Means: The engineer is not left of the chess lover. So "not anywhere to the left of" means engineer is not left of chess lover; i.e., engineer is either at same position (if same person) or to the right. Since there are only two positions, possibilities: If engineer is at position 2 and chess lover at position 1, then engineer is to the right => satisfies (not left). If engineer at position 1 and chess lover at position 2, engineer is left => violates. If engineer and chess lover are same person, then engineer is not left (they are same position) => satisfies. So constraint: NOT(engineer_position < chess_position). Equivalent: engineer_position >= chess_position.

2. "The person who likes cooking is somewhere to the left of the person who is thai". Means cooking lover position < thai person position. So cooking is left of thai.
